_what_this_is: The vintage we KNOW we have, per source in src/sources.py, plus how to ask
the publisher whether they now have something newer. scripts/check_freshness.py
reads this file, fetches each source's metadata over HTTPS, and exits non-zero
for every source whose upstream is newer than the vintage recorded here.
When it fires, there are exactly two honest responses, and both are edits:
1. ingest the new release and bump the vintage here in the same change; or
2. decide not to ingest yet and bump the vintage anyway, with a note —
the git diff of this file IS the record that the release was seen.
Silencing the check any other way recreates the failure it exists to catch:
the bond layer ran two years stale with a green test suite the whole time.
Methods: 'socrata' compares the portal's rowsUpdatedAt/viewLastModified to
vintage_utc; 'page_year' extracts years from the publisher's own download
page with `pattern` and compares the max to vintage_year; 'next_url' probes
the URL the NEXT release would have (a 200 with non-HTML content means it
shipped); 'etag' watches a published file's ETag/Last-Modified for change;
'unverifiable' is an explicit admission that the source offers no signal,

tea_peims.meaning: Latest fiscal year ingested. The page describes its own coverage as '2009-2025 Summarized PEIMS Actual Financial Data'; when fiscal 2026 lands that end year moves.

tea_snapshot.meaning: Latest Snapshot year ingested. The download page lists one 'Snapshot YYYY' link per release.

tea_staar_district.meaning: Latest school year in data/staar_district_long.csv (SY 2024 and 2025). The page titles its releases 'YYYY-YYYY STAAR ...'.

tea_property.meaning: Latest certified tax year ingested. 'Tax Year YYYY' is the page's own label for each release; bare years on this page are nav and copyright noise, so the pattern must keep the words.

tea_recapture.meaning: Latest fiscal year of the excess-local-revenue district list ingested (register covers 1994-2026). The page links each release as 'YYYY-YYYY-excess-local-revenue-districts'.

tea_accountability.meaning: We ingested the 2025 Enhanced Statewide Summary; the URL is year-pinned, so the 2026 release will appear at the sibling URL probed here. A 200 serving a spreadsheet means it shipped. After ingesting it, point this at 2027.

census_tiger.meaning: Boundaries on the map are TIGER2024; Census publishes each vintage at a predictable path, so this probes the next one. After moving to TIGER2025, point this at TIGER2026.

bond_elections.meaning: Ingested first-party from data.texas.gov on 2026-08-11 (4,992 decided propositions). The portal's metadata API reports rowsUpdatedAt for the dataset itself; anything after this date is data we have not seen.

brb_debt_outstanding.meaning: The Board's issuer index carries no updatedAt field, so this watches the file's own ETag (an S3 content hash: it moves only when the bytes move). Ingested 2026-08-11, fiscal 2025 actuals. If this fires repeatedly with no new fiscal year visible, the index is churning and the method should be revisited before it teaches anyone to ignore it.

bls_cpi.meaning: Dynamic page: no Last-Modified, no ETag, no dataset metadata API. CPI-U annual averages change once a year in mid-January; the constant-dollar base year (2024) is pinned deliberately and does not track releases.
